newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish public sector owes state PLN 3 bln - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Polish public sector owes state PLN 3 bln - finmin.

text.p: The Polish public sector's institutions, such as schools and hospitals, owe the treasury about three billion zlotys, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Friday.
PAP news agency quoted Belka as telling parliament that the state-owned health sectors' debt amounted to 2.2 billion zlotys while educational institutions owed some 750 million zlotys.
Belka was quoted as saying that the debt has mounted partly due to leniency of the treasury, which in the past wrote off the debts.
"Write-offs encouraged the process, because it created the feeling of impunity," Belka was quoted as saying.
The ministry has earlier said that the debts do not pose a threat for this year's national budget.

The minister addressed parliament following allegations that the national budget suffered losses because private firms had been buying the public sector's debts and using them, as allowed by law, to meet their liabilities to the treasury.
Belka said it was impossible to estimate how much the budget had lost as a result of the process.
The government's watchdog, the Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) earlier said the practice has cost the budget at least 100 million zlotys ($33 million).

NIK said heads of hospitals have been buying equipment from domestic and foreign suppliers, knowing the state has not budgeted for such acquisitions, however necessary, and the hospital could not pay.

NIK said the supplier would then sell the hospital's debt to other firms -- sometimes abroad -- who wait for punitive interest rates to build up, until finally someone buys and uses the now-inflated debt to settle tax bills under a government scheme designed to help debt-ridden public institutions.
The finance ministry has stopped the procedure by suspending the provision on settling taxes with debts of the public sector's institutions.
